Cabinets That Hold Up to Florida Humidity: Materials, Finishes, and Outdoor Kitchens

Key takeaways

  • Humidity makes wood and wood-based boards swell and shrink; sealed edges and the right finish matter as much as the material.
  • Kitchens near sinks and dishwashers, bathrooms, and laundry rooms need the most moisture protection.
  • Outdoor kitchens need weather-resistant materials made for sun and rain, not indoor cabinets moved outside.

What humidity does to cabinets

Tampa Bay air is humid most of the year. Wood and wood-based panels absorb that moisture and release it again, which can lead to swelling, warped doors, peeling edges, and doors that stop closing evenly. The damage almost always starts at unsealed edges and around the sink.

What to look for indoors

  • Sealed edges on every panel, including the ones you do not see.
  • A durable finish on doors and boxes, not only on the visible faces.
  • Extra protection under the sink and next to the dishwasher, where leaks and steam hit first.
  • Good ventilation in bathrooms and laundry rooms, so cabinets dry out between uses.

Outdoor kitchens are a different category

An outdoor kitchen on a Florida lanai lives with sun, rain, and salt air. It needs materials designed for outdoor use and hardware that resists corrosion. Indoor cabinets moved outside will not last, even under a roof.

PalmCraft builds outdoor kitchen cabinetry from durable, weather-resistant materials and plans the layout around your grill, fridge, and sink.

Questions to ask any cabinet maker

  • What are the boxes and doors made of, and how are the edges sealed?
  • What finish do you recommend for this room, and why?
  • What does the warranty cover, and for how long?
  • For outdoor kitchens: which materials and hardware are rated for outdoor use?
